title: Archi-Agents: Approximating the architectural design process with collaborative specialized multi-agent system LLM and Building Information Modeling
task: 多智能体BIM方案生成与协同优化
inputData: 自然语言设计需求 + IFC/BIM模型 + 空间、成本与性能知识库
contribution: 提出Archi-Agents，以Project Architect、Architectural Programmer、Cost Engineer和Energy Analyst等专门智能体协同完成建筑方案生成与迭代，并结合BIM知识图谱、多视角向量知识库和RAG支持空间、成本、能耗与用户需求的综合决策。
abstract: Architectural design requires collaboration across spatial functionality, cost efficiency, energy performance and user preferences. Archi-Agents introduces a specialized multi-agent LLM system integrated with a multi-perspective vector knowledge base and BIM. Role-differentiated agents collaborate iteratively to generate and refine BIM-based design solutions from natural-language requirements while incorporating spatial, cost and performance information.
methodology: The framework organizes specialized LLM agents into a Chatchain-enabled collaborative workflow. IFC models are processed with ifcOpenShell and transformed into simplified BIM knowledge graphs and semantic JSON, while a multi-perspective knowledge base supports hybrid retrieval over structured numerical/categorical information and semantic vector embeddings. Agents retrieve relevant spatial, cost, and performance knowledge, propose and negotiate design changes, and a Revit-oriented parametric refactoring/interface component applies design transformations and exports updated BIM/IFC models. Human designers can intervene during the iterative process.
results: The paper reports a prototype design-generation demonstration rather than a quantitative benchmark. The workflow shows specialized agents retrieving spatial, cost, and energy information and producing/refining a BIM design through a Revit-oriented interface. The authors explicitly note limitations: the current knowledge base mainly covers conceptual spatial layers; materials, structures, furnishings, and regulation/code information are incomplete; the training/data basis is limited; and simplified space, cost, and energy calculations constrain accuracy. The evidence should therefore be read as proof-of-concept rather than validated performance superiority.
taskEn: Multi-agent BIM design generation and collaborative optimization
inputDataEn: Natural-language design requirements plus IFC/BIM models and spatial, cost, and performance knowledge bases
operationEvidence: Archi-Agents retrieves structured and semantic BIM knowledge through its hybrid knowledge base, generates and negotiates design modifications across specialized agents, and applies the resulting parametric transformations through a Revit/BIM interface to produce updated model outputs.
